s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A1.definition: Conditions that narrow the claim to a region: what the evidence actually covered (sample, materials, task, setting, version, observed conditions, stand-ins) and what the authors declared as the target or ruled out.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A1.exclusion_rule: A statement about applying the approach elsewhere is BC-A2.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A1.inclusion_rule: The condition restricts where the claim holds.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A1.label: Stated bounds of the claim

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A2.definition: Conditions facing outward: applicability asserted or suspected for analogous cases, advice on where the approach pays off or should not be used, and named variations, moderators, populations or properties left untested.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A2.exclusion_rule: A restriction on the tested region is BC-A1.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A2.inclusion_rule: The condition concerns cases the evidence did not cover.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A2.label: Reach claimed beyond the evidence

availability.message: No source-bound examples are linked to this distinction in the current gallery snapshot. Missing coding does not establish absence of the mechanism or activity.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A3.definition: The approach is said or shown not to work in a case inside its own region: stated incapacity under a named condition, or observed attenuation or failure in a tested case.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A3.exclusion_rule: Doubt about reach without a demonstrated failure is BC-A2 (BC021).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A3.inclusion_rule: A break inside the claimed scope.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A3.label: Failure inside the claimed scope

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A4.definition: Content present but not a boundary condition, or an empty value stating no condition at all.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A4.exclusion_rule: Anything that bounds, extends or breaks the claim.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A4.inclusion_rule: The value carries no scoping force.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-A4.label: Not a boundary condition

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C01.definition: What the evidence actually covered: the dataset or stimuli, the study sample, the task and protocol, eligibility gates, setting and duration, the tested version, an empirically observed condition under which the effect held, a simulated or proxy stand-in, the measured performance envelope.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C01.exclusion_rule: A target the authors declared rather than exercised is declared scope (BC-C02).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C01.inclusion_rule: A fact about the evidence base.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C01.label: Demonstrated scope

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C02.definition: What the authors say the work is for or requires: target task or content, required input format, target users, explicit exclusions, declared capacity limits, target domain, language or culture, an explicit refusal to generalise, a dependency on an outside expert, required user competence.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C02.exclusion_rule: What was actually tested is demonstrated scope (BC-C01).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C02.inclusion_rule: A choice or requirement stated by the authors.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C02.label: Declared scope

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C03.definition: Asserted applicability to analogous cases, conditions under which the approach is most useful, a hedged transfer belief, and deployment contexts the authors advise against.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C03.exclusion_rule: A named untested condition flagged as a gap is hedged but untested (BC-C04).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C03.inclusion_rule: The authors speak about cases beyond the evidence.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C03.label: Conditional extension

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C04.definition: Generalisation flagged as uncertain, a named variation deferred to future work, an untested moderator, an untested population, a property left unverified for want of a measure.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C04.exclusion_rule: A confident outward claim is conditional extension (BC-C03).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C04.inclusion_rule: A gap in reach named and left open.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C04.label: Hedged but untested

availability.message: No source-bound examples are linked to this distinction in the current gallery snapshot. Missing coding does not establish absence of the mechanism or activity.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C05.definition: Stated incapacity under a named condition, or observed attenuation or failure in a tested case.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C05.inclusion_rule: A break inside the claimed region.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC-C05.label: Failure inside the claimed scope

s1:boundary_conditions:BC013.definition: Something the authors name and then rule out of the contribution: dimensions not addressed, aspects deliberately set aside, functionality not supported. Framed as a boundary of the claim, not as a failure (BC030) or a future plan (BC020).

s1:boundary_conditions:BC014.definition: What the data must look like for the method to run: tabular wide format, finite-range variables, SVG charts, available source data, a high-quality reference set. A structural assumption baked into the technique.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC014.label: Required input format, data type or precondition

s1:boundary_conditions:BC015.definition: An asserted ceiling on how much the approach handles: number of dimensions, outcomes, results, concurrent users, beyond which it degrades. Stated as a design bound, not measured performance (BC007).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC015.label: Declared capacity, scale or perceptual limit

s1:boundary_conditions:BC016.definition: The authors state outright that the finding is not offered as general: results apply only to this population, no claim of generalizable theory, parameters not claimed broadly. A meta-statement about claim strength.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC017.definition: The claim is bounded to particular languages, scripts, regions or cultural contexts: English-only inputs, Cantonese study, Chinese primary-school essays, US-based sample by design. Linguistic-cultural envelope specifically.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC018.definition: The claim depends on something the approach does not supply itself: expert oversight, clinician confirmation, administrator permission, collaboration with data scientists. A dependency on outside authority or labour.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC018.label: Holds only with an external expert, permission or human in the loop

s1:boundary_conditions:BC019.definition: What a user must already know or be able to do for the approach to work: chart literacy, Python and notebook familiarity, statistical training, domain expertise as a floor. A skill precondition on people, distinct from who the work is for (BC010) and from a dependency on an outside authority or collaborator (BC018).

s1:boundary_conditions:BC020.definition: A specific extension the authors flag and explicitly leave for later: other models, other tasks, longitudinal use, multi-turn settings. Named, not exercised, and framed as a plan rather than a doubt (BC021).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC020.label: Named variation deferred to future work

s1:boundary_conditions:BC021.definition: The authors warn the result may not transfer: findings may not generalize to harder tasks, results may differ on other platforms, caution when extending. Direction is doubt about reach, without a demonstrated failure.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC021.label: Generalization flagged as uncertain

availability.message: No source-bound examples are linked to this distinction in the current gallery snapshot. Missing coding does not establish absence of the mechanism or activity.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC022.definition: A named variable the authors believe would shift the effect but did not manipulate: task difficulty, motivation, expertise, stakes, age, form factor. The condition is identified as consequential and left unexercised.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC022.label: Untested moderator suspected to change the result

s1:boundary_conditions:BC023.definition: A group the claim was not exercised on but is acknowledged as relevant: assistive-technology users, novices, other stakeholders, practitioners rather than students. About people specifically, left untested.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC023.label: Untested population or stakeholder group

s1:boundary_conditions:BC024.definition: A named property of the claim cannot be checked because no ground truth, benchmark or accepted measure exists, so the authors flag the gap and proceed. Direction is unverified reach, not a demonstrated failure (BC031) and not a deferred plan (BC020).
s1:boundary_conditions:BC024.label: Claim left unverified for want of ground truth or a measure

availability.message: No source-bound examples are linked to this distinction in the current gallery snapshot. Missing coding does not establish absence of the mechanism or activity.

s1:boundary_conditions:BC030.definition: The approach is said to be unable to work in a specific case: cannot help if the source is inaccessible, cannot be used with multiple viewers, does not translate to that display class. Structural failure, argued rather than measured.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC030.label: Stated incapacity under a named condition

s1:boundary_conditions:BC031.definition: Measured or observed evidence that the effect weakened, vanished or broke down in a case actually exercised: null result for a subgroup, effect limited when inputs are similar, a baseline that stayed competitive.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC031.label: Observed attenuation or failure in a tested case

s1:boundary_conditions:BC040.definition: An outward claim that the approach also works elsewhere, stated with confidence: can also be applied to other sports, not specific to captioning, extendable to other datasets given a stated condition. Widens rather than restricts.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC040.label: Asserted applicability to analogous cases

s1:boundary_conditions:BC041.definition: An outward claim softened by belief or speculation: we suspect the findings generalize, we believe the approach applies in principle, it may benefit other populations. Outward-facing and explicitly unverified.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC041.label: Hedged or speculative transfer belief

s1:boundary_conditions:BC042.definition: Guidance on where the approach pays off best: particularly valuable for high-stakes decisions, ideal when data has enough facets, a good choice when slow selection is tolerable. A recommendation profile, not a restriction on the evidence.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC042.label: Conditions under which the approach is most useful

s1:boundary_conditions:BC043.definition: Where the authors say the approach should not be used: safety-critical systems, domains with unclear fairness standards, settings where errors carry safety consequences. Outward-facing caution about future application.
s1:boundary_conditions:BC043.label: Deployment contexts the authors advise against

s1:evidence:EV-A1.definition: The warrant is the paper's own words about its system: describing what a view, interaction, algorithm, encoding, schema, workflow or prompt is or does; depicting it in a figure or worked example; asserting a benefit, implication or argument for it; or demonstrating it without evaluation.
s1:evidence:EV-A1.exclusion_rule: A description of the study procedure is EV-A2; an observed or measured result is EV-A3.
s1:evidence:EV-A1.inclusion_rule: No one outside the authors, and no measurement, stands behind the claim.
s1:evidence:EV-A1.label: The authors' own account

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:evidence:EV-A2.definition: The warrant describes how evidence was gathered: the procedure participants followed, the conditions manipulated, the materials or instruments, the coding procedure, the controls against bias.
s1:evidence:EV-A2.exclusion_rule: An outcome attributed to a condition is EV-A3 (EV024).
s1:evidence:EV-A2.label: Study apparatus, not a result

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:evidence:EV-A3.definition: The warrant is something observed or measured: a finding with participants, including negative ones; or a technical, benchmark or data result.
s1:evidence:EV-A3.exclusion_rule: A formative finding that only motivated the design is EV-A1 (EV036).
s1:evidence:EV-A3.inclusion_rule: A result, from people or from data, stands behind the claim.
s1:evidence:EV-A3.label: Empirical results

availability.message: No source-bound examples are linked to this distinction in the current gallery snapshot. Missing coding does not establish absence of the mechanism or activity.

s1:evidence:EV-A4.definition: The warrant is borrowed: prior work cited for the technique or a definition, an external standard or taxonomy adopted, or a stated departure from prior work.
s1:evidence:EV-A4.exclusion_rule: The authors' own argument without citation is EV-A1 (EV038).
s1:evidence:EV-A4.inclusion_rule: Someone else's work or scheme licenses the claim.
s1:evidence:EV-A4.label: Cited external authority

availability.message: This code records information not specified in the source. It is kept for evidence completeness.

s1:evidence:EV-A5.definition: The locator and quotation are present but say nothing that supports the claim: a pointer that only asserts existence, or quoted text unrelated to the claim.
s1:evidence:EV-A5.exclusion_rule: An asserted benefit is a weak warrant, not an absent one (EV009 in EV-A1).
s1:evidence:EV-A5.inclusion_rule: The record carries no usable evidence.
s1:evidence:EV-A5.label: No evidence at the cited location

s1:evidence:EV-C01.definition: Prose stating what the person can do, how something is computed, what a component contains, how data map to marks, the shape of an artifact, the design rationale, the workflow, the prompt text or a parameter value.
s1:evidence:EV-C01.exclusion_rule: A claim that it helps, with nothing shown, is an asserted warrant (EV-C03); a figure or scenario is depiction (EV-C02).
s1:evidence:EV-C01.inclusion_rule: The authors describe what they built and why.
s1:evidence:EV-C01.label: The system as the authors describe it

s1:evidence:EV-C02.definition: A worked example or usage scenario narrated by the authors, a figure, screenshot or table cited as the depiction, or an appendix or supplementary artifact.
s1:evidence:EV-C02.exclusion_rule: A demonstration offered as the whole warrant with no evaluation is an asserted warrant (EV014 in EV-C03).
s1:evidence:EV-C02.inclusion_rule: The mechanism is shown rather than measured.
s1:evidence:EV-C02.label: Figures and illustrations

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:evidence:EV-C03.definition: A benefit asserted without demonstration, a design implication or future possibility, a formative finding that motivated the design, a conceptual or normative argument, or a demonstration explicitly without evaluation.
s1:evidence:EV-C03.exclusion_rule: A negative or disconfirming result is empirical (EV037 in EV-C04).
s1:evidence:EV-C03.inclusion_rule: The authors vouch for the mechanism without showing a result.
s1:evidence:EV-C03.label: Asserted or argued only

s1:evidence:EV-C04.definition: Aggregated qualitative findings, observed behaviour, verbatim quotes, quantified responses, expert or stakeholder feedback, deployment records, statistical tests, and negative, limiting or disconfirming results.

s1:evidence:EV-C04.inclusion_rule: People used or judged the mechanism and the outcome is reported.

s1:facet:FC-A1.definition: Operations in which the system renders meaning so a person can inspect it: why an output came out as it did, where a claim came from, what content amounts to, and in what perceptual form it is shown.
s1:facet:FC-A1.exclusion_rule: Not arranging or relating several things (FC-A2), not letting the person change anything (FC-A3), not telling the person what to do or how they are doing (FC-A4).
s1:facet:FC-A1.inclusion_rule: The system produces something to look at or listen to that stands for meaning already present in the material, the model or the source.
s1:facet:FC-A1.label: Explanation and visibility

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:facet:FC-A2.definition: Operations that impose structure on material or bound what is in view: arranging, grouping, mapping, comparing, filtering, ranking, holding and recalling.
s1:facet:FC-A2.exclusion_rule: Not the rendering of one thing (FC-A1), not the person changing the thing itself (FC-A3), not advice, feedback or pacing (FC-A4).
s1:facet:FC-A2.inclusion_rule: Two or more items are placed in a relation (spatial, temporal, hierarchical, similarity, correspondence, contrast) or the set in view is narrowed, ordered or kept.
s1:facet:FC-A2.label: Organisation and comparison

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:facet:FC-A3.definition: Operations in which the person states, shapes, chooses, corrects, steers or tries out meaning: specifying intent, manipulating a representation, choosing among offered candidates, probing or rehearsing.
s1:facet:FC-A3.exclusion_rule: Not the system deciding what the person should do (FC-A4) and not passive inspection (FC-A1).
s1:facet:FC-A3.inclusion_rule: The person is the one who changes state: authoring a constraint, editing a draft, picking an option, setting a dial, running a what-if.
s1:facet:FC-A3.label: User control and expression

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:facet:FC-A4.definition: Operations in which the system directs, assesses, paces, structures or prompts the person's work: pointing, warning, recommending, giving feedback, releasing help in stages, ordering the work into steps, asking the person to articulate.
s1:facet:FC-A4.exclusion_rule: Not the person's own action (FC-A3) and not a neutral rendering of content or reasoning (FC-A1).
s1:facet:FC-A4.inclusion_rule: The system takes the initiative about the person's conduct of the task: what to attend to, what to do next, how well it went, when help arrives, what stage comes next, what to say.
s1:facet:FC-A4.label: Guidance and feedback

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:facet:FC-A5.definition: Operations whose object is other people: making others' state and judgment visible, taking another vantage, building a representation together, structuring deliberation, controlling disclosure, framing roles.
s1:facet:FC-A5.exclusion_rule: Human-AI division of labour, handoff and orchestration stay in workflow structure (FC-C16): they organise the work, not the people.
s1:facet:FC-A5.inclusion_rule: The semantic object is a person, a group or the relation among them rather than content, a model or the system.
s1:facet:FC-A5.label: Collaboration and perspective

availability.message: Source-bound examples are available in the current gallery snapshot.

s1:facet:FC-C01.definition: Makes a system's outputs, behaviour, uncertainty or current state inspectable, so people can understand what it is doing and judge its results.

s1:facet:FC-C01.inclusion_rule: The thing made legible is the system or model itself.
s1:facet:FC-C01.label: Explaining system behaviour

s1:facet:FC-C02.inclusion_rule: The operation anchors meaning in its origin or lets a person get from a derived thing to the thing it was derived from.
s1:facet:FC-C02.label: Sources and evidence

s1:process_before:PB-A1.definition: The before-state is a procedure people carried out without the scaffold: gathering, reading, labelling, producing, judging, iterating, expressing what they wanted, coordinating with others.

s1:process_before:PB-A2.definition: The before-state is what the person's tools and signals failed to give them: limited or generic tools, automation that could not be steered, expertise gates, lost state, opaque or coarse output, no feedback, no provenance, information absent from the world.
s1:process_before:PB-A2.exclusion_rule: The person's unaided effort is PB-A1 even when tools were poor; a named prior system evaluated as such is PB-A3.
s1:process_before:PB-A2.inclusion_rule: The described deficit belongs to the environment (tool, system output, available information), not to the person's own activity.

s1:process_before:PB-A3.definition: The before-state is a state rather than a workflow: a published method or system named as the state of the art, the authors' own superseded prototype, a prior framing of the problem, or how people were disposed or behaved.
s1:process_before:PB-A3.exclusion_rule: A prior system used as an experimental comparator is PB-A4.

s2:affected_capability:HC-A1.label: Judging and governing the system

s2:affected_work_activity:WA055.definition: The activity is retrieving facts, procedures or other already held information from internal memory for the current task. External cues may trigger retrieval, but the information being obtained is internal rather than read from an external store. Retrieval alone is not evidence of learning, practice or durable retention.
exclusion_rule: Searching documents or an external information source (WA012).
Reading information off a display (WA009).
Acquiring or rehearsing knowledge to get better (WA028).
Transforming remembered information to derive a result (WA056).
inclusion_rule: Retrieving facts and procedures from memory.
The retrieval component of a phrase that separately names retrieval and mental computation.

s2:affected_work_activity:WA056.definition: The activity is internally operating on remembered or mentally represented information to derive a result, such as mental calculation or transformation. s2:lineage_named_construct:LN117.definition: The explicitly attributed constructionist tradition treats learners’ design and construction of meaningful external products as a way of constructing knowledge. exclusion_rule: An explicitly named object to think with when that specific object-role construct is the value (LN113).
Generic constructivism or knowledge construction without constructionism/artifact-making attribution.
Production of an artifact by itself, without a cited constructionist account.
Whole-tradition attribution inferred solely from citing Papert’s name.
inclusion_rule: Papert’s constructionism explicitly named in Harel’s learner-as-designer account.
An attributed constructionist rationale for learner creation of software or other meaningful external artifacts.
s2:lineage_named_construct:LN117.label: Constructionist learning through artifact making

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN118.definition: The cited account organizes composing into named sequential stages, such as pre-writing/writing/re-writing or conception/incubation/production. Its use may be supportive or critical; stance remains separate.

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN118.inclusion_rule: Rohman and Britton composition-stage models explicitly named by the citing source.
s2:lineage_named_construct:LN118.label: Staged accounts of composing

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN119.definition: The cited account treats revision as repeated re-seeing or reworking during composition, rather than an exclusively terminal repair stage.
s2:lineage_named_construct:LN119.exclusion_rule: Generic reflection in/on action (LN081); editing controls without a cited account; an end-stage writing model.

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN120.definition: The explicitly named ICAP or DOLA framework classifies passive, active, constructive and interactive engagement through overt learning activity and relates the modes to a hypothesized learning order. An empirical application of the same explicitly named taxonomy remains the same lineage construct.
exclusion_rule: Any unnamed four-condition experiment.
Generic cognitive engagement, motivation or metacognition without the named taxonomy.
Instructional design frameworks defined by knowledge components and alignment of objectives/assessment (LN100).
Treating store/integrate/infer/co-infer as directly verified cognitive processes.
inclusion_rule: The DOLA/ICAP named taxonomy and its four-mode distinctions.
A cited four-mode comparison explicitly linked by its source-node evidence to the ICAP hypothesis.
s2:lineage_named_construct:LN120.label: ICAP/DOLA overt-engagement taxonomy

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN121.definition: The explicitly attributed construct concerns whether a person can establish that a candidate answer is correct. Its cited psychology form includes one group member convincing others to switch to a correct solution on an intellective problem; the citing paper connects this to verification of AI recommendations.
exclusion_rule: The absence of an independent correctness oracle (LN084).
Appropriate reliance or complementary performance as a target outcome rather than the attributed demonstrability construct (LN002).
A generic explanation method or an inference that a person learned verification.
inclusion_rule: Explicitly named demonstrability linked to checking answer correctness.
The attributed social-combination/intellective-problem account reused to frame recommendation verification.
s2:lineage_named_construct:LN121.label: Demonstrability of a correct solution to a person or group

s2:lineage_named_construct:LN122.definition: The source explicitly attributes a structural-equation or causal-intervention account, including an intervention described as changing a variable while preserving the relevant causal structure. s2:support_form:SF-A1.definition: Forms in which the system tells the person something: a recommendation, ranked set, label, alert, confidence or risk score about a case, or an account of why and how it behaves, where its content came from, what it is doing and what it cannot do.
s2:support_form:SF-A1.exclusion_rule: Material generated for the person to work from is SF-A2; an instrument the person operates on the system is SF-A3.
s2:support_form:SF-A1.inclusion_rule: The support is a statement the system makes to the person about a case or about itself.
s2:support_form:SF-A1.label: The system's judgement and its account of itself

s2:support_form:SF-A2.definition: Forms that place content in front of the person to read, handle, keep or work from: generated drafts, alternatives, summaries, questions and replies; visualizations, canvases, linked views, comparisons, highlights, structured renderings and shared artifacts; physical, bodily and multimodal forms; and the records, annotations and adaptations that persist across a session.
s2:support_form:SF-A2.exclusion_rule: A statement about a case or about the system is SF-A1; a control or prompt the person operates is SF-A3; a structure imposed on the process is SF-A4.

s2:support_form:SF-A2.label: Material and representations put before the person

s2:support_form:SF-A3.definition: Forms through which the person acts on the system: prompts, templates, region-scoped instructions, examples and generation settings that direct what is generated; direct manipulation, parameter, accept-reject-override, selection, scope, undo and constraint controls.
s2:support_form:SF-A3.exclusion_rule: Content the system offers back is SF-A2; a step the process requires of the person is SF-A4.

s2:support_form:SF-A4.definition: Forms that shape how the person works rather than what they see: staged workflows, forms to fill, checklists and rubrics, reflective prompts, worked examples, conceptual frameworks, graduated support that fades, collaboration scripts, built-in verification steps, friction, and deliberate openness that makes the person supply meaning.

s2:support_form:SF-A5.definition: Forms in which the support is a relation rather than an interface element: feedback, review, facilitation or aggregated signals from other people; the system's own social conduct as a repairing or embodied agent; and standing arrangements of roles, allocation between person and system, oversight, deployment and incentives.
